steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the core multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: Secure funding and recruit or assign the four core posts through Digital and IT from September through November 2026: 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, 1.0 FTE Product & Service Designer and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer. All four posts are required throughout the three-year mobilisation and are intended to transition into Digital and IT business-as-usual establishment from July 2029. Mobilisation costs are pro-rata in Year One and full-year in Years Two and Three. Mark Peace is Product Owner. Confirm approximately 0.2 FTE protected Business Analysis and approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, with up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if the senior engineering post cannot carry that function. Establish ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling as a three-year engineering capability, currently profiled at £90,000 in each mobilisation year pending commercial validation.

outputs.title: Senior Backend & Integration Engineer mobilised
outputs.summary: 1.0 FTE senior engineer responsible for backend services, domain/API integration, technical integration with King’s systems and senior engineering judgement. Planning grade assumption: King’s Grade 8. Confirm separately whether this post also fulfils solution architecture.

outputs.title: Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer mobilised
outputs.summary: 1.0 FTE hands-on engineer delivering student-facing Hub and King’s Edge features and the supporting application services, working under the technical direction of the senior engineer. Planning grade assumption: King’s Grade 7.

outputs.title: Product & Service Designer mobilised
outputs.summary: 1.0 FTE designer combining UX and interaction design, UI design, service and journey design, prototyping, student/user research and usability testing across the shared Hub and King’s Edge experience. Planning grade assumption: King’s Grade 7.

outputs.title: QA Engineer mobilised
outputs.summary: 1.0 FTE quality engineer responsible for product test strategy, automated and manual QA, regression and release quality. Planning grade assumption: King’s Grade 6. The start date may be offset until code production is established, which would reduce actual Year One spend against the eight-month planning estimate.

outputs.title: Lean shared-capacity model confirmed
outputs.summary: Confirm approximately 0.2 FTE protected Business Analysis and approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support. Add up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer cannot carry it. Draw specialist security, privacy, accessibility, data, architecture assurance and service-management input from existing institutional functions as required rather than creating standing fractional posts.

outputs.title: Agentic-development capability established
outputs.summary: Confirm the commercial route for ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling across the three-year mobilisation. The planning allowance is £90,000 in each year, with actual spend reduced if Digital and IT can provide equivalent reliable shared capacity more economically.

outputs.title: KAI technical-asset assessment
outputs.summary: Inventory reusable KAI technical components, including Azure AI Foundry capability, and make explicit adopt, adapt or retire decisions against the target Hub architecture rather than transferring the existing team or product model wholesale.

existingCapacity.owner: Existing or seconded institutional capability, organisational home to be confirmed
existingCapacity.contribution: Map systems, information flows, ownership, dependencies, operational implications and readiness across priority journeys. Working protected allocation: approximately 0.2 FTE during the main discovery period.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Critical estate, ownership and dependency evidence may remain incomplete or be absorbed unsustainably by the Product & Service Designer.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide Azure, environments, deployment pipeline, observability and related platform support without assuming a full-time DevOps post in the core. Working protected allocation: approximately 0.2 FTE.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Engineering delivery and release may be blocked or create unsupported operational arrangements.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT / James Costerton to confirm
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide solution-architecture authority only where this cannot credibly be carried within the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer post. Working allocation if separately required: up to approximately 0.2 FTE.
existingCapacity.periodNeeded: Before architecture is locked and thereafter at material design points
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The programme may create avoidable coupling, unsupported design decisions or an architecture gap between the Hub and wider institutional platforms.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT and other relevant institutional specialists
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide time-bound security, privacy, accessibility, data, architecture-assurance and service-management input when required. Product testing and release-quality ownership remains with the QA Engineer.
existingCapacity.periodNeeded: At relevant design, assurance and release points
existingCapacity.confidence: existing specialist capacity to be scheduled
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The product may reach release points without the specialist institutional assurance required for safe operation.

yearlyProfile.note: Eight-month mobilisation cost, November 2026 to June 2027

newInvestment.estimatedCost: £243,000 three-year planning estimate in constant 2026 prices: £61,000 for November 2026 to June 2027, then approximately £91,000 in each full year. Assumes King’s Grade 8 at the current salary-range midpoint, plus employer on-costs. Final grade, appointment point and future pay awards require Digital and IT / HR validation.
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before role creation and recruitment begins
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Education strategic investment / SCIF route, transferred to Digital and IT for recruitment and delivery
newInvestment.fundingStatus: Unfunded; business-case approval and role grading required
newInvestment.rationale: Provides the senior backend, domain/API integration and systems-integration capability required throughout mobilisation to replatform King’s Edge, establish and evolve shared Hub foundations, and support deeper integration. Digital and IT must confirm whether solution architecture is also carried by this post.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The team lacks senior technical integration capability and the Edge replatform and Hub foundations are unlikely to proceed safely at the planned pace.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: £200,000 three-year planning estimate in constant 2026 prices: £50,000 for November 2026 to June 2027, then approximately £75,000 in each full year. Assumes King’s Grade 7 at the current salary-range midpoint, plus employer on-costs. Final grade, appointment point and future pay awards require Digital and IT / HR validation.

newInvestment.fundingRoute: Education strategic investment / SCIF route, transferred to Digital and IT for recruitment and delivery
newInvestment.fundingStatus: Unfunded; business-case approval and role grading required
newInvestment.rationale: Provides sustained hands-on feature delivery across the student-facing Hub, King’s Edge and supporting application services throughout the three-year mobilisation.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The senior engineer becomes the sole substantive developer, creating a throughput and resilience bottleneck.

yearlyProfile.note: Eight-month planning baseline; a later Year One start would reduce actual spend

Assumes King’s Grade 6 at the current salary-range midpoint, plus employer on-costs. A later QA start would reduce actual Year One spend. Final grade, appointment point and future pay awards require Digital and IT / HR validation.
newInvestment.periodNeeded: November 2026 to June 2029 planning profile; Year One start may be offset once sustained code production begins
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before role creation and recruitment begins
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Education strategic investment / SCIF route, transferred to Digital and IT for recruitment and delivery
newInvestment.fundingStatus: Unfunded; business-case approval and role grading required
newInvestment.rationale: Provides dedicated ownership of product test strategy, automated and manual QA, regression and release quality throughout mobilisation. Specialist security, privacy, accessibility and architecture assurance remain institutional specialist functions rather than being transferred wholesale into this role.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: £270,000 three-year planning allowance: £90,000 in each mobilisation year for ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling. The amount is based on the 28 August Digital and IT discussion of the likely cost of a dedicated instance and remains subject to commercial validation. Reliable shared institutional capacity should reduce actual spend where it provides equivalent capability.
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before initial tooling commitment and at annual renewal points
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Digital Student Experience Hub three-year mobilisation business case
newInvestment.fundingStatus: Included in three-year mobilisation baseline; commercial validation required
newInvestment.rationale: Provides sustained agentic-development capacity so the experienced engineering team can use agentic software development throughout mobilisation while retaining human specification, review and accountability. It is budgeted separately from Azure/environment/platform costs and is not a substitute for the core engineering posts.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The programme loses a material engineering-productivity capability that Digital and IT identified as important to the delivery model.

enablingConditions.condition: Approve the four core posts and Digital and IT recruitment route in time for mobilisation, with three-year mobilisation funding profiled and an explicit commitment to transition the four experienced posts into recurrent BAU establishment from July 2029. The planning grade assumptions are Grade 8 for Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, Grade 7 for Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, Grade 7 for Product & Service Designer and Grade 6 for QA Engineer; Digital and IT / HR should validate these before final business-case submission.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation leadership with Digital and IT
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The core team may be treated as temporary project capacity, weakening recruitment and creating an avoidable cliff edge at the end of mobilisation.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm Mark Peace as Product Owner and validate the lean shared-capacity model: approximately 0.2 FTE Business Analysis, approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, and up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if not carried by the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer. Specialist institutional assurance is scheduled on demand rather than represented as standing FTE.
enablingConditions.owner: James Costerton / Digital and IT with Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation lead
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before mobilisation and resource commitments are finalised
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The business case may fund the core team without securing the small amount of additional institutional capacity needed to make it effective.

enablingConditions.condition: Validate the commercial structure for the £90,000 annual agentic-development planning allowance, including whether existing Digital and IT shared capacity can reduce actual incremental cost while preserving reliable project access across all three mobilisation years.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before initial tooling commitment and at annual renewal points
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The business case may reserve more cash than ultimately required or the team may mobilise without the sustained agentic-development capability assumed in the delivery model.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm the workforce route for establishing the four core Digital and IT roles on terms compatible with their planned transition into BAU after June 2029, while keeping mobilisation funding and recurrent funding visibly distinct.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with Education, Finance and strategic investment governance
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Fixed-term recruitment constraints may reduce hiring quality and leave a recurrent capability with an unnecessary end-of-programme staffing cliff edge.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish one transparent pipeline, prioritisation and capacity cadence, proportionate discovery and user involvement led through the Product & Service Designer, engineering and quality expectations, sustained agentic-development practices, embedded assurance and release practices across King’s Edge and the Digital Student Experience Hub.

outputs.title: Demand intake and prioritisation
outputs.summary: Create one transparent route for new demand, triage, sequencing and capacity decisions.

outputs.title: Capacity and trade-off rules
outputs.summary: Make King’s Edge commitments, Hub build, broad discovery and available capacity visible, with explicit decisions when new scope would displace agreed work.

outputs.title: Proportionate discovery and user involvement
outputs.summary: Use the Product & Service Designer’s integrated research, service-design and prototyping capability, supported by Business Analysis where needed, at the level required by the decision rather than applying a fixed heavyweight lifecycle.

outputs.title: Engineering, quality and assurance practices
outputs.summary: Agree practical code review, automated and manual testing, documentation, QA ownership and routes into specialist institutional assurance.

outputs.title: Agentic-development operating practice
outputs.summary: Define which backlog work should be accelerated through the funded agentic tooling, how senior engineers specify and review that work, and how productivity, defects and rework will be measured across the mobilisation.

outputs.title: Release discipline
outputs.summary: Define proportionate criteria for controlled release, support readiness and learning from live use.

steps.title: Prove the capability through King’s Edge, broad discovery and the focused Hub release
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, prove that the funded core and lean shared-capacity model can deliver the substantive King’s Edge roadmap and focused Digital Student Experience Hub release while integrated product/service design and proportionate Business Analysis map the wider estate and priority journeys. Use evidence to refine the operating model before introducing the planned supervised junior-engineering placement in Year Two.

outputs.title: Substantive King’s Edge delivery
outputs.summary: Move the replatform and agreed richer Edge capabilities predictably through build, test and controlled release.

outputs.title: Focused Digital Student Experience Hub delivery
outputs.summary: Deliver the shared home and agreed first-release journeys without turning the first year into several parallel deep integration programmes.

outputs.title: Broad discovery evidence
outputs.summary: Use the Product & Service Designer’s integrated service-design and user-research capability, supported by Business Analysis where needed, to create the wider-Hub roadmap.

outputs.title: Capability and tooling evidence
outputs.summary: Measure throughput, quality, defects, rework, discovery demand, integration effort, specialist dependencies, live-service obligations and the contribution from agentic development to inform the Year Two operating model and supervision plan.

enablingConditions.condition: Before Year Two, define the supervision, backlog boundaries, learning objectives and recruitment route needed for a sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack Engineer to add capacity without carrying critical delivery responsibility.
enablingConditions.owner: James Costerton / Digital and IT with the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The placement may either fail to add useful capacity or place inappropriate delivery responsibility on a student.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make operating practices routine across the live Digital Student Experience Hub and King’s Edge product domain, balancing roadmap delivery, incidents, maintenance, quality, discovery and continuous improvement. Add one supervised sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack Engineer during 2027/28 as additional delivery and learning capacity alongside, not instead of, the four-post experienced core.

outputs.title: Routine pipeline and capacity cadence
outputs.summary: Maintain a transparent backlog and regular prioritisation and capacity decisions across product demands.

outputs.title: Predictable discovery and release rhythm
outputs.summary: Establish a repeatable cadence balancing discovery, delivery, quality, release and evaluation.

outputs.title: Live-service feedback loop
outputs.summary: Connect incidents, support evidence, maintenance and service performance directly into product prioritisation.

outputs.title: Ownership and handover model
outputs.summary: Clarify when the product team retains responsibility, collaborates with service owners or transfers enduring capabilities.

outputs.title: Junior engineering placement test
outputs.summary: Host one full-time sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack Engineer on a supervised, lower-risk backlog to test productive junior contribution, learning value, use of agentic tooling and the potential talent-pipeline model.

yearlyProfile.note: One paid sandwich-year placement; planning employment envelope
One paid sandwich-year placement; planning employment envelope

newInvestment.estimatedCost: £70,000 two-year planning envelope: £35,000 in each of Years Two and Three for one full-time sandwich-year placement student per year. The envelope is intended to cover a competitive paid student wage plus employer/administrative on-costs. Exact employment route, duration and rate require validation with Digital and IT, HR and the relevant placement arrangements.
newInvestment.periodNeeded: One placement in 2027/28 and one placement in 2028/29
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Digital Student Experience Hub three-year mobilisation business case
newInvestment.fundingStatus: Planned from Year Two; employment route and exact cost to validate
newInvestment.rationale: Adds supervised junior delivery capacity once the experienced team and engineering practices are established, while testing whether King’s can create an effective student-to-digital-talent pipeline. The placement is augmentation and must not substitute for the Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer or other experienced core posts.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Core delivery remains viable, but King’s loses the planned test of junior engineering contribution and an opportunity to develop a repeatable internal talent pipeline.

enablingConditions.condition: Agree a formal paid sandwich-year placement route, meaningful learning objectives, supervision capacity and a bounded lower-risk backlog before recruiting the first student.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with the relevant King’s placement and HR functions
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The placement may not meet either delivery or student-learning expectations.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices where the wider roadmap justifies it
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, use live-service evidence and the first placement year to refine the capability model. Continue the planned sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack placement for a second year in 2028/29, while requiring evidence for any staffing above the four-post core plus this supervised placement capacity.

outputs.title: Evidence-led capability model
outputs.summary: Set any capability above the four-post core and planned junior placement against confirmed roadmap demand, throughput, quality, discovery needs and live-service evidence.

outputs.title: Balanced delivery and live-service capacity
outputs.summary: Plan explicitly for new development, maintenance, support, technical improvement, discovery and assurance.

outputs.title: Placement-model evidence
outputs.summary: Evaluate productive contribution, supervision cost, learning quality, agentic-tooling use and retention/talent-pipeline potential from the first placement and improve the second-year model.

enablingConditions.condition: Any staffing above the already profiled four-post core and one annual junior placement, or any further specialist requirement, must be approved from evidence and a costed roadmap within the strategic mobilisation envelope.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital Student Experience Hub governance with Digital and IT and Finance
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before additional staffing plans are fixed
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Future capacity may be treated as predetermined rather than evidence-led.

steps.title: Transition the core capability into business as usual
steps.summary: By the end of the three-year mobilisation, transition the original four experienced posts into enduring Digital and IT business-as-usual establishment, with an indicative recurrent staffing run-rate of approximately £304,000 per year in constant 2026 prices. Complete the sustainable professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with SED product ownership and Digital and IT specialist/platform services. Use mobilisation evidence to decide separately whether agentic tooling and the junior-placement model should also continue beyond June 2029.

outputs.title: Four-post core transitioned to BAU
outputs.summary: Move the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, Product & Service Designer and QA Engineer from mobilisation funding into recurrent Digital and IT establishment without a staffing cliff edge.

outputs.title: Recurrent funding route confirmed
outputs.summary: Secure the recurrent budget and workforce arrangements needed to sustain the 4.0 FTE core from July 2029, currently estimated at approximately £304,000 per year before future pay awards.

outputs.title: Enduring governance and decision rights
outputs.summary: Confirm authority over the pipeline, capacity, methods and escalation routes.

outputs.title: Professional leadership and career routes
outputs.summary: Embed role development, professional standards, mentoring, progression and learning from the sandwich-year placement model.

outputs.title: Stable specialist and service interfaces
outputs.summary: Confirm how the team works with architecture, data, integration, assurance, service management, SED product owners and other contributing teams.

outputs.title: Mobilisation experiments reviewed for BAU
outputs.summary: Decide from evidence whether agentic tooling, the annual sandwich-year placement model and any additional specialist capacity should join the four-post core in the recurrent operating model.

newInvestment.item: BAU transition: four-post digital product core
newInvestment.estimatedCost: Approximately £304,000 annual recurrent staffing run-rate in constant 2026 planning prices for the four experienced core posts: Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, Product & Service Designer and QA Engineer. Future pay awards and final appointment points will change the cash requirement.
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before 2029/30 recurrent budgets and workforce plans are fixed
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Digital and IT recurrent business-as-usual establishment / institutional operating budget
newInvestment.fundingStatus: Planned BAU transition; recurrent budget route to confirm
newInvestment.rationale: The original four experienced mobilisation posts are intended to become the enduring institutional digital product capability after the three-year mobilisation. This recurrent run-rate is deliberately separated from the three-year mobilisation investment so it is visible without being double-counted.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: King’s would build a functioning product capability and then create an avoidable staffing and service-continuity cliff edge just as the Hub moves into mature live operation.

enablingConditions.condition: Secure recurrent Digital and IT establishment and budget for the original four experienced posts from July 2029. The strategic direction is continuation into BAU; the remaining work is to confirm the recurrent funding route, final role grading and organisational arrangements, not whether the core capability survives.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with Education, Finance and institutional investment governance
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before 2029/30 recurrent budgets and workforce plans are fixed
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The programme reaches the end of mobilisation without the recurrent funding needed to retain its core institutional capability.

enablingConditions.condition: Use live evidence to decide whether agentic tooling, the sandwich-year placement model and any capability above the four-post core should also be funded recurrently after June 2029.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with Digital Student Experience Hub governance and Finance
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before post-mobilisation recurrent budgets are fixed
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Temporary mobilisation experiments may either disappear despite proven value or become recurrent commitments without sufficient evidence.
